analysis: The method `convertTimestampToZone` has two branches: legacy conversion (when `legacyConversion` is true) and non-legacy conversion. In the legacy branch, an inner try-catch handles the checked `ParseException` from `DateFormat.parse()` by wrapping it into a `RuntimeException` and rethrowing. However, other statements in this branch may throw uncaught runtime exceptions: `TimeZone.getTimeZone(ZoneId)` throws `NullPointerException` if the zone argument is null (call 6), and `Timestamp.setNanos()` throws `DateTimeException` if the nanos value is out of range (call 4). In the non-legacy branch, `convert()` and `LocalDateTime.ofInstant()` and `Timestamp.ofEpochSecond()` may each throw `DateTimeException` (calls 3,7,8) if the timestamp or instant is out of supported range. None of these runtime exceptions are currently caught. The existing pattern of wrapping `ParseException` into `RuntimeException` suggests that all conversion failures should be handled uniformly: by catching any exception and throwing a `RuntimeException`. To minimize changes and add only one try-catch structure, the best plan is to wrap the entire method body in an outer try-catch that catches `Exception` (covering both checked `ParseException` and runtime exceptions) and throws a `RuntimeException`. The inner try-catch for `ParseException` can then be removed, since the outer catch will handle it. This ensures all exceptions are handled consistently.
